next_step: Send scaled benchmark report and proposed Dedicated capacity layout; follow up with infra VP
notes:
Summary: Late-stage procurement stalled and moved to closed-lost after vendor selection. Primary reason: technical fit on throughput and burst capacity + internal budget freeze.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2025-09-01: Initial SDR inbound (warehouse automation RFP). quick discovery call.
- 2025-10-14: Demo (chat + routing) with AE, SE. Showed baseline latencies on standard workloads.
- 2025-11-30: POC kickoff — small cluster (4xA100) provisioned in Dedicated trial.
- 2026-01-15: Fireflies call (ff_20260115_4567) — infra raised concerns about queueing under morning peak bursts.
- 2026-02-05: Stress test results posted to drive; observed p95 tail latency spikes and dropped requests when burst >700 rps. (see /drive/proposals/...).
- 2026-02-10: Infra deep-dive with SE (ff_20260210_8732). Requested deterministic p95 <200ms under 800 qps sustained.
- 2026-02-20: Procurement tells AE "cost too high for Dedicated commitment; competitor can guarantee throughput with hybrid on-prem appliance."

POC details / technical notes:
- Workload: extremely bursty (morning gate open, ad-hoc reroutes). Typical steady-state 120-200 rps, bursts to 600-900 rps for 2-8 min windows.
- Redwood trial config: 4xA100 equivalent Dedicated pool, autoscale test enabled, KV prefix cache enabled. Observed queueing when concurrency >150 active chat sessions; burst handling produced queue growth and token timeouts.
- Meridian requirement: consistent p95 <200ms for routing decisions; tail behaviour is critical (can't accept occasional 2-5s tail spikes).
- Requested features: guaranteed concurrency lanes, hard SLAs on tail latency, ability to reserve burst capacity and predictable billing model for bursts.
- Security: requires VPC deployment + SOC2 + enterprise KMS. Also asked for audit log retention 3+ years and data residency US-only.

Sales notes / conversation snippets:
- "We need something that doesn't surprise our customers on the dock — 1s late is a pile-up." — VP Infra.
- AE attempted commercial: flexible Dedicated + burst burst pool. Procurement: "price out of band relative to our capex plan."
- SE recommended Private on-prem node for critical lane, but procurement pushed back on integration effort and timeline.

Why deal stalled / closed-lost:
- Technical fit: Meridian judged Redwood's Hosted + Dedicated trial couldn't guarantee sustained burst capacity without expensive reserved headroom. The POC exposed queueing patterns under realistic bursts and the infra team lost confidence.
- Commercial: procurement freeze and unwillingness to commit to high monthly Dedicated minimums. Competing vendor offered an on-prem inference appliance with firm throughput SLA at comparable TCO for their 3-year plan.
- Organizational: champion in infra left before procurement; no replacement champion to push for private deployment.

Next internal actions (for Redwood):
- Capture full POC artifact set and test logs (RDINF-6421/6610).
- Build a short "burst handling/guarantees" playbook with example capacity layouts and cost profiles for similar customers.
- Re-engage in 6-9 months if procurement re-opens or if infra champion returns.

Disposition: Closed-lost to competitor (not committed). Will watch for re-engagement signals (RFP reissue, headcount change).
